A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same asynchronous RLHF work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TLDR experiments on off-policy robustness, scaling, and computational efficiency, plus LLaMA 3.1 8B instruction-following experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds original GSM8k, asynchronous PPO, and RLOO robustness results.

M1.justification: The asynchronous pipeline, Online DPO objective, and best/worst-of-K selection are retained. Appendix B newly specifies Proximal RLOO with importance weighting and PPO clipping. However, v1 underspecifies its RLOO implementation and Figure 4 is unchanged, leaving uncertainty about whether this changes the procedure or documents a variant already used.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8k mathematical reasoning alongside the retained TLDR summarization and No Robots instruction-following tasks. Generating reasoning traces and obtaining exact-answer correctness rewards substantially extends coverage beyond preference-based evaluation.

E2.justification: The No Robots comparison expands from synchronous/asynchronous Online DPO to include synchronous/asynchronous PPO (Table 9). Appendix B adds an evaluated CoPG-style RLOO comparator against Proximal RLOO. These change comparator membership within experiments, even though PPO already appeared in v1's TLDR comparisons.

E3.justification: The added GSM8k experiments introduce Rho-1B, binary correctness rewards, greedy pass@1 evaluation, four sampled completions per prompt, and a 4-L40s setup (Section 5.2; Table 10). Added chatbot PPO experiments use a KL coefficient of 0.01. The retained TLDR and chatbot Online DPO hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the CoPG/Proximal RLOO staleness comparison in Figure 13, qualitative GSM8k checks of completion counts and selection, and a detailed generation/training overhead analysis in Appendix A.3. Figure 14 adds backend timing comparisons across model scales. The original off-policy, scaling, and compute-allocation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated training runs or seeds, or reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added figures and tables continue reporting results without error bars.

E6.justification: New GSM8k results report synchronous/asynchronous Online DPO at 52.2%/52.6% pass@1 and 218/129 minutes (Table 2). New PPO chatbot and CoPG robustness results also substantially expand the findings. Original Figures 1-9 and the 57.2% chatbot win rates are retained. Added chatbot runtimes conflict: Table 1 gives 230/142, whereas Table 9 gives 213.04/154.03 for synchronous/asynchronous Online DPO.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a focused mathematical comparison of RLOO and CoPG gradients, derives the importance-weighted RLOO gradient, and defines the clipped objective in Equation 1. v1 contains no corresponding derivation; the existing RLHF and Online DPO mathematics remains unchanged.

C1.justification: v1 only conjectures applicability to reasoning. v2 adds an abstract and introduction contribution claiming approximately 70% faster asynchronous GSM8k training with matching accuracy. Its conclusion also explicitly qualifies competitiveness by acknowledging that optimized synchronous libraries likely outperform the presented implementation.

C2.justification: v2 adds proposed explanations for PPO's optimization and computational disadvantages, reasoning-task efficiency without a reward model, and synchronous backend memory, integration, and maintenance costs. It newly acknowledges stronger optimized synchronous implementations and VinePPO's higher GSM8k accuracy at greater cost. The original GIL and communication discussion is relocated, rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 supplies GSM8k hyperparameters and hardware details, additional runtime measurements, explicit RLOO implementation mathematics, and asynchronous pseudocode in Appendix D. A new reproducibility statement reports released baseline checkpoints and training datasets and integration into open-instruct. The code link and original experiment hyperparameter tables were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against CoPG's off-policy formulation and detailed discussion of NeMo-Aligner, TensorRT-LLM, and DeepSpeed-Chat. GSM8k, Rho-1, and VinePPO references establish a new reasoning comparison context, while Tulu 3 is cited as subsequent adoption. These extend the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most existing background, TLDR, and optimization prose remains substantially unchanged. Local revisions reshape the abstract, contribution list, scaling section, and conclusion; move the practical-runtime subsection into Appendix A.2; and add a reproducibility statement and appendix organization. The expanded scientific content does not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 10-14, new comparison and hyperparameter tables, and Algorithm 1. Figure 9 moves to Appendix A.2, while main-text Table 1 redisplays existing chatbot scores with a runtime column. All nine original figure images are retained unchanged, but the added displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's speculative reasoning extension into a tested GSM8k result and verifies asynchronous training with PPO at 8B scale, substantially strengthening evidence beyond preference rewards and Online DPO. Added protocols, pseudocode, and implementation information improve reproducibility, while the conclusion better qualifies competitiveness. Conflicting chatbot runtimes in Tables 1 and 9 and Figure 10's speedup caption weaken numerical consistency, but the broader empirical support and technical transparency provide a substantial net improvement.
